rites.name: Torukak
rites.text: Torukak is the concept of the rising heat that gathers in the first roots of Drorkaigok during the Singing, when the world's foundations take shape under the flames of the Holy Age. It is remembered in the temples as the force that teaches orders to hold their ground against the burning tide.

rites.name: Saseth
rites.text: Saseth is a concept in Drorkaigok, a principle of threshold and patience that the Courts of the Martial Realm name whenever a council weighs a door between worlds. Its shape is a bargain kept over seasons rather than a single blow, held by the groves that first sheltered the sovereign's growing kingdoms.

rites.name: Seollus
rites.text: Seollus is a concept in Drorkaigok, the quiet thread the makers spin during the Seeding, when the Weave is planted and its powers lie dormant among the growing groves. It belongs to the Age of the first sovereign, when kingdoms are young and their strength is measured in harvests rather than wars.

rites.name: Raulus
rites.text: Raulus is the concept of the Seeding in Drorkaigok, the moment the makers plant the Weave and the quiet powers fall into sleep. It belongs to the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke the old bonds between peoples and their lands.

rites.name: Morudoren
rites.text: Morudoren is the concept of the Shattered Vow, the oath-fire that bound the broken worlds of Drorkaigok together after the Sundering. Its temples taught that a sworn word could hold a falling sky, and its orders kept the flame lit through the long ages of the Shards.

rites.name: Braron
rites.text: Braron is a concept held within Drorkaigok's Walled Age, a notion of the wall as a living oath that orders and churches tended for centuries. It came to shape the first crossings and the groves that grew beside the early kingdoms of the first sovereign.

rites.name: Fenastene
rites.text: Fenastene is the concept of a long wall-keeping discipline in Drorkaigok, a practice in which the order's holders stand fast against pressure and hold their ground for centuries. It is remembered as the art by which the first crossings of the Walled Age were made possible, with each holder's oath set into the stone of the gates.

rites.name: Toraigokurn
rites.text: Toraigokurn is a corrosive current of hungry sorcery that seeps through the seams of Drorkaigok's martial orders, offering practitioners ruinous strength in exchange for flesh that slowly twists and rebels. Its adepts are feared as much for the ruin they bring upon themselves as for the storms they call down. Old war-academies still teach its warnings through scarred instructors who carry their own mutations as lessons.

rites.name: Torougoth
rites.text: Torougoth is the silver-grey pulse that seeps between the shard-worlds of Drorkaigok, gathering in lattices where the tides of the Grand Loom run thin. Sages draw it through tuned glass to kindle lanterns, sky-rails, and the tireless forge-hearts of the river cities.

rites.name: Grimoktar
rites.text: Grimoktar is a discipline of battle-chant and ember-binding practiced in the Martial realm, drawing its strength from a fierce crimson current that roars through the lower stratum of Drorkaigok. Its adepts kindle forge-flares in their palms, harden the resolve of allied warriors with heated war-songs, and scorch the ranks of their foes with bursts of living cinder.

rites.name: Goukurn
rites.text: Goukurn is a discipline of spellcraft in the martial realm of Drorkaigok, taught in the third age to duellists who would rather bend the strength of their foes than match it. Practitioners draw on drifting currents of mineral breath to loosen the plates of armour, reshape common stone and iron, and temper blades with glimmering alloy. Its scholars regard it as a craft of patience rather than of raw destruction.

rites.name: Grurkun
rites.text: Grurkun is a lantern-rite of the Drorkaigok Martial era, in which practitioners bind spiraling kelp-light to their palms and sing it into the bones of the injured. Its keepers mend broken soldiers, coax hollow trunks back into living timber, and wrap marching companies in a shimmering tide that deflects blades and blunts falling stones.

rites.name: Karazhuktar
rites.text: Karazhuktar is a hunting-rite drawn from the restless currents of Drorkaigok's high plains, where practitioners call down the pack-spirits of the grasslands. Those who master it gain sharpened senses, bristling hides, and the ability to command migrating herds of wild beasts. Elders warn that the rite slowly reshapes its users into the predators they summon.

rites.name: Kathairkoth
rites.text: Kathairkoth is a disciplined art of drawing on the Gale of Vevraun, a restless wind that lifts veils from buried truths and burns through falsehood like dry grass. Its practitioners ward themselves in layered gusts and can scour a whole valley of concealment in a single breath.

rites.name: Vhairnogun
rites.text: Vhairnogun is a sanctioned discipline of the Martial realm in Drorkaigok, practiced by scarred duellists who channel the ceaseless pressure of their own battle-fury into layered strikes. Its masters teach that a warrior who has fought a thousand times carries a reservoir of resolve that can be spent in a single act. Its oldest forms are said to split hills when the swordsman is pushed past their endurance.

rites.name: Kornuthok
rites.text: Kornuthok is a shadow-weaving discipline practiced by the Veilmoot of Drorkaigok, who bind their breath to the drifting grey winds of the eastern marshes. Its adepts can dissolve their outlines into the dusk and turn the minds of foes against themselves, then strike from a shadow that was never there. Elders warn that a practitioner who inhales too deeply of the wind may never fully return to the light.

rites.name: Guthak
rites.text: Guthak is an ancient martial discipline in Drorkaigok, drawn from the teachings of cloud-wardens who bind the high tempests into fighting form. Its practitioners strike with storm-blade and thunder-fist, and in the last age of the wardens they could split peaks with a single cut.

rites.name: Drarnouzhok
rites.text: Drarnouzhok is a forbidden discipline of coiled hexes that channels a caster's unstable inner rot into bursts of ruin, mutating flesh and splitting stone alike. Each invocation risks sloughing the practitioner's own body into something wretched, so only the desperate and the gifted attempt it.

rites.name: Torazhurn
rites.text: Torazhurn is a martial discipline in the Drorkaigok omniverse, practiced by duelists who read the tremor of fate before blades meet. Its adepts bend the odds of a single clash, turning a stray gust or a loose stone into a decisive blow. The art was born in the third age of the era as a way to hold ground against larger foes.

rites.name: Vhouthogar
rites.text: Vhouthogar is a martial art of the Drorkaigok, practised by ash-blooded duelists who hang lantern-fungus from their wrists and cultivate creeping rot as a weapon. Its masters can seep a wasting blight into an opponent's blood, dulling their strength while sharpening the resilience of the adherents of their own bloated saints.

rites.name: Draithar
rites.text: Draithar is a veil-weaving discipline of the Gloamtide Choir, drawing on the slow pull of hidden undercurrents to bind foes in drifting silk and shelter comrades in pockets of stilled water. Its practitioners sing the tidal refrains that hold a battlefield's flow in their favour, though the craft demands costly memory from each singer.

rites.name: Kroggurkoth
rites.text: Kroggurkoth is a standing war-ward woven from the last breaths of fallen soldiers, which hangs over a battlefield and keeps answering threats long after its maker has died. Its strands crawl across the ground to strike at anything that crosses a chalked boundary, and it can only be unpicked by the same oath that first bound it.

rites.name: Grimougukok
rites.text: Grimougukok is a concept of endless warding, a standing pendulum of pressure that the old duel-wardens of Drorkaigok keep swinging across their courts. Its sweep never fully stops, so each pass answers the last with a breath of force that shoves whatever stands in the arc.

rites.name: Kukarnar
rites.text: Kukarnar is a martial discipline in Drorkaigok, practiced by wanderers who bind spinning gear-sigils to their wrists and let them drift through the air around them. Within its reach, rival fighters find their limbs lurching between haste and sluggishness, their bodies aging or unaging in patches as the sigils turn. The school is prized less for raw force than for its uncanny control of the rhythm of a duel.

rites.name: Gurnarkok
rites.text: Gurnarkok is a drifting lattice of gray-lit wisps that hum low in the marrow of its allies' bones, its power a patient haze rather than a blow. Its age is three and it belongs to the martial powers of an era six, where it is prized for distracting and wearing down enemies. It can unmake a stone outcrop slowly by weathering it away.

rites.name: Groktar
rites.text: Groktar is a veil of drifting ash-gold motes woven by the Drorkaigok monks of the Ember Loom to hold the ashes of fallen oath-keepers aloft. It hangs over battlefields as a slow, patient shroud, dimming the wills of those beneath it. It is said to remember every breath it has ever stilled.

rites.name: Kokugun
rites.text: Kokugun is a martial spell-form in the Drorkaigok, a ghostly pair of ivory jaws that lash out from the caster's shadow to rend foes. Those caught are pulled into a churning grey hollow that gnaws at them until they are gone from the field. Its power is modest but relentless, scaling with each sustained breath of the practitioner.

rites.name: Voruktun
rites.text: Voruktun is a binding rite of the Martial realm's sixth era, drawing spectral fetters from the bones of defeated duelists to lock opponents in place. Each chain siphons strength from the bound while the rite endures, feeding the caster's reserves. Its authors held that a battlefield sealed by such fetters is a city-sized crucible of stored force.

rites.name: Karuktun
rites.text: Karuktun is a standing ward of drowned light that the Tarnveil scholars of Drorkaigok keep woven above contested ground, its folds able to draw a caster's stored force through and redistribute it to allied rites. Its strength is measured less by what it breaks than by how much it can hold without tearing.

rites.name: Grimoukturn
rites.text: Grimoukturn is a shimmering haze of jade-winged swarm-motes that drifts through the ruins of the Vallen Reach, knitting torn flesh shut while stripping vigor from anything that is not kin to it. Its hum is said to be the sound of seeds splitting open in the dark. It is counted among the oldest weapons of the Hollow Concord, and no one has yet found a way to end it.

rites.name: Vhothak
rites.text: Vhothak is a ruin-engine born from a shattered aurora in the Drorkaigok marches, a spiraling knot of unmade light that unpicks the nerves of anything near it. It thrives on disorder, sharpening its reach each time the surrounding ground splits or the air screams with panic.

rites.name: Kouktairnun
rites.text: Kouktairnun is a standing veil of prismatic radiance that the war-chanters of the Ashen Choirs weave across contested ground, holding back foes and sheltering the line behind it. Its shimmering panels bend shot and stamp aside any who press against them, and the chant that sustains it is said never to stop until the field is quiet.

rites.name: Thokairkun
rites.text: Thokairkun is a rolling tide of grave-soil that a Martial-realm caster raises from the bottom of the world, burying foes in cold loam until their breath stops. Where the soil passes, forgotten dead claw up out of the earth to march beneath the banners of the living.

rites.name: Kraktozhoth
rites.text: Kraktozhoth is a sustained tempest of crackling sorcery that the wardsmiths of Vorhalen Reach bound into a single unbroken gale. It sweeps across the battlefield, flaying armor and hurling soldiers aside, and it has never once been seen to pause.

rites.name: Vhoguktoth
rites.text: Vhoguktoth is a standing ward of the Drorkaigok martial schools, a bronze-horned ember bull woven from heated wind that thunders across the fields to drive raiders from the grain. Its flame scorches whatever it passes, though the bull is said to lose strength the longer it runs unchallenged.

rites.name: Drairkaggun
rites.text: Drairkaggun is the slow tempering of a fallen warrior's essence within a sealed foundry of the Drorkaigok realm, where a new vessel is cast around what remains. Each cycle the forge burns away a sliver of the original self, so the returned champion is steadier but quieter in memory.

rites.name: Thagun
rites.text: Thagun is the iron-rimmed ember that smoulders in the ribs of Drorkaigok's sky-wardens, a kindling of stored thunder that answers only to oaths sworn at dawn. It is said to scour rot and hollow malice from any creature it touches, leaving only the bare will beneath.

rites.name: Drokturn
rites.text: Drokturn is a ritual turning of the bloodied oath-wheel, performed by the war-priests of the Drorkai to beseech their ancestors for aid. Its answer may mend a broken limb, lend strength to a warrior's arm, or hurl a withering wave of fire against enemies.

rites.name: Gaizhok
rites.text: Gaizhok is a grim craft of hollowing out the soul-threads of the departed and weaving them into marionette bodies that march at the will of a practitioner. Its adepts gather in cold crypts where the air grows thick with the scent of old graves and stilled breath. Each raised corpse drinks a little of the living world's warmth to keep its shambling form moving.

rites.name: Vhaggoktoth
rites.text: Vhaggoktoth is a discipline of bending the flow of duration, practised in secret by a handful of wizards who guard their methods jealously. Its adepts can hasten allies into bursts of tireless motion, age a foe's body into brittle decay, or coax a fresh wound to unknit itself back into the moment before it was struck.

rites.name: Thaktar
rites.text: Thaktar is a volatile green-burning power drawn from refined star-iron in the Martial realm of Drorkaigok. Its wielders gain fierce heat and reach, but the substance corrodes their own flesh with every surge.

rites.name: Drouthaigun
rites.text: Drouthaigun is a volatile discharge of hunger-bright sparks drawn from the burning cores of the Drorkaigok deep-warrens, harnessed by cunning gnaw-priests and clanwork tinkers. Its crackling arcs leap from foe to foe with terrible force, yet the bolts routinely wrack the hands that loose them, leaving whole chambers scorched and stinking.

rites.name: Karouthun
rites.text: Karouthun is a shifting ember-spirit of the Drorkaigok omniverse, woven into the Martial realm's cults of change. Its heat unmakes flesh and reknits it into unstable new shapes, so that a burned victim often walks away wearing a different form than the one they had. Practitioners prize it for its chaos, though it rarely obeys them for long.

rites.name: Gouzhok
rites.text: Gouzhok is the bargain-crowned state a warrior reaches when their chosen dark power finally claims them, turning their body into a living engine of ruin bound to a distant master. Its wielder can unleash blows that flatten hills and crack the ground for leagues, yet every triumph feeds the master who holds the leash.

rites.name: Ilosaoma
rites.text: Ilosaoma is the concept of the Drorkaigok forge-tempering, a principle that binds a single blade's temper to the choice of which future it will be struck in. In the Three Futures it is the thread the Library uses to file each branching ending onto its own shelf.

rites.name: Tarneldon
rites.text: Tarneldon is a concept in Drorkaigok, a principle that the Three Futures teach as the seed of every branching ending, shelved in the Library during the Holy Age of flame and temple orders. Its adherents describe it as a spark that decides which path a flame will take when the ending forks.
